4851-history-of-the-united-netherlands-1:
Treachery at Deventer dominates this 1587 volume, and John Lothrop Motley traces how Leicester's rule bred betrayal. Barneveld's sway grows as Leicester's servants gossip and plot. The quarrel between Norris and Hollock deepens the earl's ill will toward his own officers.

Stanley, made governor of Deventer, heeds Leicester's secret orders. He brushes off Wilkes's protests. Then, after a banquet, he hands the city to the Spanish chief Tassis. York's double-dealing runs beside the bargain. Motley follows the weak defense of Stanley's conduct and the fates of both men, showing how private deals rotted a public cause.
history-of-the-united-netherlands-1587a:
John Lothrop Motley gives chapter thirteen of his History of the United Netherlands to Barneveld's rising influence. The Advocate's authority grows as Leicester's unpopularity deepens. A modest young man appears under their joint tutelage: Prince Maurice, who could bide his time. He learns in field and cabinet, Motley writes, the great lessons of the age.

Hohenlo, a desperate fighter, teaches Maurice war; Barneveld, a profound statesman, teaches him government. The chapter is a portrait of an apprenticeship that would rule the republic for decades. Around it, the English governor's party intrigues and fades. Motley's structure is biographical inside the political narrative. Two old men, the soldier and the lawyer, form the third figure of his history. Readers who follow Maurice's later mastery should start here, where the pupil still listens more than he speaks.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1437a:
Section 1437a of Title 2 of the United States Code requires training and education programs in congressional employing offices. It sits in Chapter 24 of Title 2, the Congressional Accountability Act, current through Public Law 119-134. The programs teach staff the rights the Act gives them.

Each employing office must develop and run a program to train and educate its covered employees. The teaching covers the rights and protections given under the chapter. It also covers the procedures open under subchapter IV for hearing claims of breaches of the chapter. Each office must report to two committees on how the program is carried out. The report goes to the House Administration Committee and the Senate Rules and Administration Committee. It is due not later than forty-five days after the start of each Congress, from the one hundred seventeenth Congress onward.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1817a:
Section 1817a of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with surplus property of the Architect of the Capitol. The Architect runs the buildings and grounds of the Capitol complex. Property that office no longer needs must still be handled under set rules.

The section gives the Architect power to dispose of surplus or obsolete personal property. The allowed routes are transfer to another agency, donation, sale, trade-in, or discarding. Money from a sale or trade-in goes back into funds for the Architect's operations. Those funds may pay for property of the same or a similar kind. They stay open for use in the year received and the year after. A closing rule makes the section apply from fiscal year 2010 onward.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1907a: Section 1907a of Title 2 of the United States Code gives the Capitol Police a funds power. The power is to move money between two pots in a fiscal year. One pot is for salaries of the force that year. The other pot is for its general costs that year. The rule first held for fiscal year 2014. A move needs the nod of the Appropriations panels of both houses first.
uslaw-usc-t2-s287a:
Section 287a of Title 2 of the United States Code vests the running of the Office of the Parliamentarian in the Parliamentarian of the House. The Speaker appoints the Parliamentarian. The choice must be made without regard to party ties. Fitness to perform the duties of the post is the sole test named in the text.

Whoever is appointed serves at the pleasure of the Speaker. The section sits in Chapter 9C of Title 2, on the Office of Parliamentarian of the House of Representatives. The hosted text is the Code as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. It is current through Public Law 119-134. Readers get, in a few lines, who runs a key advisory office of the House, how that officer is chosen, and on what terms the officer holds the job.
uslaw-usc-t2-s907a:
Section 907a of Title 2 provides a suspension route for deficit rules in war or low growth. Its opening procedures turn on a low-growth report from the Congressional Budget Office. Whenever that office issues such a report under the provision cited, a trigger follows for the majority leaders of both Houses.

The House Majority Leader may, and the Senate Majority Leader shall, introduce a joint resolution. The resolution declares that the conditions specified in the text are met. It suspends the relevant provisions of the budget titles named. The exact form of the resolution is set out in the section itself, word for word after the resolving clause. The section sits in Chapter 20 of Title 2, on emergency powers to eliminate budget deficits. The hosted Code text is current through Public Law 119-134.
